title: Canonical model pin grammar and resolver precedence
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Define a single, unambiguous pin grammar and runtime resolution algorithm that supports pin-by-commit, pin-by-semver (exact and ranges), and pin-by-tag; document SDK/REST API surface; ensure safe upgrade/fallback behavior; and wire publishing of performance profiles for pinned versions.

Background: Customers want deterministic model behavior (reproducibility) while also benefiting from guarded automatic upgrades when desired. Current behavior is fragmented across SDKs and runtime: some clients can pin to tags, some use semver, and runtime fallbacks differ between hosted and dedicated. This ticket centralizes the grammar and precedence, plus operational constraints for performance profile publishing.

Non-goals: Implementing the full runtime resolver (separate follow-ups) and UI in Console (design tickets will handle). This ticket focuses on spec, API surface, SDK examples, and acceptance tests.

Specification highlights:
1) Pin grammar (canonical string forms accepted by API/SDK):
   - commit: sha-256 abbreviated (8-12 chars) -> "commit:<hex>" e.g., "commit:3f7a9b2c"
   - semver exact -> "semver:1.2.3"
   - semver ranges -> "semver:^1.2.0" or "semver:~1.2.3"
   - tag -> "tag:stable" or simply "stable" (SDKs accept shorthand)
   - implicit latest -> absent pin or "latest"

2) Resolution precedence (highest to lowest):
   a) commit (exact hash)
   b) semver exact (1.2.3)
   c) semver range (^, ~, >= etc.) -> resolves to highest compatible published version
   d) tag -> resolves to the commit/version the tag points at at resolution time
   e) latest/unpinned -> best-effort latest verified release

   Rationale: Exact commit guarantees byte-for-byte reproducibility; semver exact is deterministic but not tied to commit; semver ranges allow controlled upgrades; tags are by definition mutable and therefore lower precedence.

3) Fallback and graceful-degradation rules:
   - If resolution by the requested pin type fails (e.g., no matching semver), resolver proceeds down precedence chain only if the request includes a fallback policy. Default policy is NO_FALLBACK for P0/P1 customers. For requests that enable fallback (flag: allow_fallback=true), resolver will attempt next precedence entries with these constraints: must match ABI/compat metadata and must have a published performance_profile within 48 hours of the target version.
   - If allow_fallback=false (default for hosted API), resolver returns 404-like error with deterministic diagnostic payload listing attempted candidates and reasons.

4) Compatibility and performance profile rules:
   - Every published model version must publish a performance_profile (latency P50/P95, GPU memory, kv-cache footprint) at the time of release. Resolver refuses a pin-to-version if a performance_profile is missing for that version unless client sets emergency_allow_unprofiled=true.
   - When resolving semver ranges or tags, the runtime prefers candidates with a performance_profile and prioritizes lower tail-latency given client SLO hint (if provided).

5) SDK/REST API surface changes:
   - New optional request fields on generation/chat endpoints: pin (string), allow_fallback (boolean string "true"|"false"), fallback_policy ("semver-only"|"tag-only"|"any"), client_slo_ms (integer as string)
   - Pin validation performed client-side in SDKs for early feedback; servers perform authoritative validation at acceptance time.
   - New admin API endpoints for publishing tags and performance profiles: POST /admin/models/:model/versions/:version/perf_profile and POST /admin/models/:model/tags -> body accepts canonical pin grammar.

6) Backward compatibility and migration: 
   - Existing unpinned calls continue to behave as before (latest).
   - Introduce a feature flag on accounts: pinned_strict_mode (default true). When true, allow_fallback defaults to false and resolver is strict. For legacy customers who relied on silent upgrades, account ops can disable pinned_strict_mode.

Acceptance criteria:
- Spec doc merged in the repository describing grammar, precedence, and examples.
- SDKs (Python/TS/Go) implement client-side pin validation and a deterministic pin->resolver RPC payload.
- Runtime has a test harness that exercises resolution precedence and fallback policy with synthetic versions and performance profiles.
- End-to-end test that attempts to resolve tag->semver->commit flows and asserts telemetry (console events) are emitted with candidate list.
- Documentation for Console and API updated with migration guide and examples.

Open questions (to be resolved in design review):
- Should semver ranges be interpreted using semver precedence only or also prefer versions with matching quantization/precision? (tentative: require model ABI compatibility annotated on release metadata)
- How to represent pinned_performance_profile signatures in signatures for replayable requests?

Implementation notes and constraints:
- The resolver must be idempotent and cache resolution results for 5 minutes per account to avoid thrashing but must invalidate cache on tag movement events.
- Performance profile publishing is rate-limited to 1 publish/minute per model in admin API to reduce noisy updates.
- Logging must include: requested_pin, resolved_version, resolution_path, and perf_profile_version. These fields are required for rollout analysis.

Test cases (high level):
- commit -> resolves commit, satisfies performance profile check
- semver exact -> resolves to exact version if exists, else error (unless allow_fallback)
- semver range -> resolves to highest compatible with published perf_profile
- tag -> resolves to current tag mapping; tag move triggers change and invalidates cache
- missing perf_profile -> reject unless emergency flag set

Migration plan:
1) Publish spec and SDK validation in a library release (runtime-1.19-beta).
2) Run canary on internal teams with pinned_strict_mode=true.
3) Provide opt-out for customers that require legacy behavior for 90 days.

comments: 2025-02-19 - Asha Kapoor: Initial draft completed and posted to team channel. Calling out the need for a strict default for enterprise customers.
2025-02-21 - Marco Ruiz: Reviewed draft; requested explicit examples for SDK call sites (Python and JS) and an error payload shape. Added to acceptance criteria.
2025-02-25 - Priya Menon (PM): Suggested adding account-level toggle (pinned_strict_mode) and migration path. Marked customer_impact as high for early adopters.

2025-02-27 - Engineering review: Agreed on precedence but asked to clarify semantics for mixed pins (e.g., semver:^1.2.0 and tag:staging provided in same request). Proposed rule: first-match evaluated left-to-right if multiple pins provided; otherwise single pin expected.
2025-03-02 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-api/pull/5021 contains draft of admin endpoints and request field changes. Waiting on unit tests for resolver cache invalidation.
2025-03-03 - Security note from SRE: performance_profile publish path must be authenticated via KMS-backed token; added to security checklist.
